title: Deep earthquake pairs had more larger-first order at seven days than at 30-365 days in 11 ComCat groups in 2000-2025
abstract: We compared magnitude order in deep earthquake pairs at short and long time gaps in a fixed ComCat snapshot for 2000-2025. Both events had depth greater than 300 km, magnitude at least 5.5, and a magnitude gap of at least 0.3. Distance was at most 200 km. Eleven graph groups had pairs in both the short window through seven days and the reference window at 30-365 days. The mean within-group larger-first share difference was 41.8 percentage points. Its conditional 95% group bootstrap interval was 14.3 to 68.2 points. An exact independent fair-sign test gave p = 0.0234. Pooled shares were 71.3% and 50.6%, a smaller 20.7-point contrast. Six groups had only one short pair. A 100-km check gave an interval that included zero, and the 7-30-day contrast was uncertain. Thus the primary contrast depends on grouping and spatial scale. It is consistent with an aftershock-like process but does not prove triggering or a recovery time. Data overlap prior campaign work. The package gives code, aggregate evidence, exact null sums, a figure, source hashes and an independent numerical audit. External event records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Short-minus-reference larger-first shares, with conditional 95% group bootstrap intervals. Checks overlap and have no multiple-test correction.
